Five parallel passes (L1 general/coding/agent boards, L2 cyber/safety boards, L3 science/robotics/multimodal boards + dataset pages, A1/A2 uncited arXiv papers); only rows the DB lacked; conflicts reported, never overwritten. Each value was checked against its saved source line before merging.

Stored value = total solves / 100 runs, summed from the published per-challenge matrix.

benchmarks.name: PutnamBench — Lean problems solved (leaderboard)
benchmarks.description: Number of PutnamBench Lean 4 problems (with answer placeholders filled) solved, as listed on the official PutnamBench leaderboard (results.json). The problem set grew over time (640 → 657 → 672); each row notes the entry date, benchmark commit and compute budget.

benchmarks.name: PhysBench (test, overall accuracy)
benchmarks.description: PhysBench (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2501.16411): 10,002 video-image-text test entries on VLM physical-world understanding across object property, relationships (spatial), scene (environment) and dynamics (phenomena). Official leaderboard overall accuracy; human 95.87.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Quality Index
benchmarks.description: AA composite for native speech-to-speech models: equal-weight mean of Big Bench Audio (reasoning), τ³-Voice (agentic voice tasks) and Full-Duplex-Bench (conversational dynamics).

benchmarks.name: SimulacraBench (NeurIPS 2026 competition)
benchmarks.description: NeurIPS 2026 competition track: predict survey responses of hard-to-reach populations on three unreleased UNHCR, UNICEF and World Bank microdata sets; code-to-data evaluation with a calibration-first normalised log score (uniform guess 0, perfect 1). Public launch 2026-08-18; no scores published yet.

benchmarks.name: RuneBench (RuneScape agent benchmark)
benchmarks.description: AI coding agents play RuneScape by writing TypeScript against an emulated game server (rs-sdk), with wiki-derived markdown knowledge files; tasks are scored by XP rate per skill within a fixed window. Framework published; no model results table yet.

benchmarks.name: MedQA (USMLE)
benchmarks.description: MedQA (Jin et al., 2021): USMLE-style multiple-choice medical exam questions (US English subset; 4-option test set is the common setting). Accuracy; variants with 5 options, 0-shot or best-of-N are stored under medqa_* ids.

benchmarks.name: LifeSciBench
benchmarks.description: LifeSciBench (OpenAI + Tacit Labs, 2026): 750 expert-authored life-science research tasks across seven workflows and seven domains, each graded against an expert rubric; problem-weighted normalized rubric score (GPT-Rosalind 0.576 in the preprint).

benchmarks.name: LifeSciBench Task Pass Rate
benchmarks.description: LifeSciBench task pass rate: share of the 750 tasks on which the model meets the pass threshold (>=70% of rubric points); GPT-Rosalind 36.1% in the preprint.

benchmarks.name: WebTailBench
benchmarks.description: Microsoft WebTailBench (Fara-7B release): 609 long-tail web tasks across 11 segments (shopping, flights, hotels, restaurants, activities, ticketing, real estate, jobs, shopping lists, comparison shopping, compositional). Stored values are the micro-average success rate from the dataset card.

benchmarks.name: OMol25 — Open Molecules 2025
benchmarks.description: Meta FAIR Open Molecules 2025 dataset and leaderboard for machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT-labelled molecular systems (fair-chem). No scores stored yet.

benchmarks.name: General365
benchmarks.description: General365 (arXiv 2604.11778): 365 diverse, challenging general-reasoning tasks; accuracy on the complete benchmark.

benchmarks.name: FinTrace (overall score)
benchmarks.description: FinTrace (arXiv 2604.10015, COLM 2026): 800 financial tool-calling trajectories scored on a nine-metric rubric; overall = mean of the nine metrics normalized to [0,1].

benchmarks.name: LiveNewsBench (human-verified test set)
benchmarks.description: LiveNewsBench (arXiv 2602.13543): agentic web-search QA on freshly curated news; human-verified test set, local agent framework (<=5 searches, <=5 page visits per question).

benchmarks.name: BURMESE-SAN
benchmarks.description: BURMESE-SAN (arXiv 2602.18788, AI Singapore et al.): Burmese NLP benchmark (NLU, reasoning, NLG, cultural tasks); MY = overall Burmese score, zero-shot.

benchmarks.name: SupChain-Bench QA (with context)
benchmarks.description: SupChain-Bench (arXiv 2602.07342): real-world supply-chain management QA; accuracy with the proprietary context documents provided.

benchmarks.name: SupChain-Bench tool calling (with SOP)
benchmarks.description: SupChain-Bench (arXiv 2602.07342): multi-step supply-chain tool calling (up to 7 tools, 30+ steps); information-retrieval accuracy when the Standard Operating Procedure is provided.

benchmarks.name: Olfactory Perception (OP) benchmark
benchmarks.description: OP benchmark (arXiv 2604.00002): LLM olfactory perception — odor classification, descriptors, intensity, pleasantness, RATA, similarity, receptor activation, smell identification; overall = unweighted mean of 8 task scores, compound-name prompts.

benchmarks.name: BeQu (Beyond Questions) knowledge-expression F1
benchmarks.description: Beyond Questions (arXiv 2605.26937): LLM knowledge expression via elicited triples; Experiment 1 overall F1 against entailment judgments (0-1).

benchmarks.name: Structured Output Benchmark (overall, coverage-adjusted)
benchmarks.description: Structured Output Benchmark (arXiv 2604.25359): multi-source (text/image/audio) structured-output quality; coverage-adjusted Overall across seven per-record metrics (0-1).

benchmarks.name: Adversarial Humanities Benchmark — overall ASR
benchmarks.description: Adversarial Humanities Benchmark (arXiv 2604.18487): attack success rate of humanities-style (stylistic) transformations of harmful prompts, EU GPAI CoP risk taxonomy; overall ASR across risks (lower = safer).

benchmarks.name: MonitorBench — CoT-only monitorability
benchmarks.description: MonitorBench (arXiv 2603.28590, COLM 2026): 1,514 instances / 19 tasks / 7 categories testing whether chain-of-thought reveals decision-critical factors; average monitorability score over tasks, CoT-only monitor scope, standard setting (Qwen3-32B monitor). Tasks refused by a model are excluded from its average.

benchmarks.name: AlpsBench Task 1 — memory extraction F1
benchmarks.description: AlpsBench (arXiv 2603.26680, SIGIR 2026): LLM personalization from real dialogues; Task 1 = personalized-memory extraction, semantic-matching F1.

benchmarks.name: AlpsBench Task 2 — memory update F1
benchmarks.description: AlpsBench (arXiv 2603.26680, SIGIR 2026): Task 2 = updating persistent memory with evolving user information, semantic-matching F1.

benchmarks.name: PrepBench — end-to-end Prep-Code accuracy
benchmarks.description: PrepBench (arXiv 2605.08687): natural-language-driven data preparation; end-to-end Prep-Code setting accuracy (Table 6 RQ1).

benchmarks.name: PanCanBench — average rubric score
benchmarks.description: PanCanBench (arXiv 2603.01343): real patient questions on pancreatic cancer, expert-rubric grading; average rubric score per model (Figure 4a; only the values named in §3.3.1 text are ingested).

benchmarks.name: LoCoBench — LCBS (LoCoBench Score)
benchmarks.description: LoCoBench (arXiv 2509.09614, Salesforce): long-context software-engineering benchmark (8 task categories, 10 languages, 10K-1M tokens); LCBS aggregate score over 17 metrics in 4 dimensions (higher is better, ~0-5 scale).

benchmarks.name: InfoOps Bench — compliance rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: Live information-operations safety benchmark (arXiv 2607.28503): share of prompts where the model amplifies or preserves a false political claim in a social-media post. Lower = more resistant.

benchmarks.name: InfoOps Bench — fact-checked rate
benchmarks.description: InfoOps Bench (arXiv 2607.28503): share of responses that fact-check the claim. Higher = better.

benchmarks.name: ORCA-bench — RCA depth (884 incidents)
benchmarks.description: ORCA-bench (arXiv 2607.28545): on-call root-cause analysis over 884 injected incidents in a microservice system (Terminus-2 harness, code + Grafana telemetry). RCA depth gives partial credit toward the root causes.

benchmarks.name: ORCA-bench — RCA accuracy (884 incidents)
benchmarks.description: ORCA-bench (arXiv 2607.28545): share of incidents where the agent names all root causes correctly.

benchmarks.name: ORCA-bench — hallucination rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: ORCA-bench (arXiv 2607.28545): share of RCA reports with hallucinated causes.

benchmarks.name: ORCA-bench Verified — RCA depth (32 tasks)
benchmarks.description: ORCA-bench Verified subset (arXiv 2607.28545, 32 human-verified incident tasks): RCA depth.

benchmarks.name: ORCA-bench Verified — RCA accuracy (32 tasks)
benchmarks.description: ORCA-bench Verified subset (arXiv 2607.28545): RCA accuracy.

benchmarks.name: MemeBench — VIKR success (closed-book, overall)
benchmarks.description: MemeBench (arXiv 2607.27798): culture-dependent meme interpretation, 1,253 memes (768 Chinese, 485 English). Success requires Visual, Identity, Knowledge and Reasoning coverage; dual-judge intersection (Gemini-3.1-Pro ∩ GPT-5.1).

benchmarks.name: MemeBench — VIKR success (English)
benchmarks.description: MemeBench (arXiv 2607.27798) English split, 485 memes.

benchmarks.name: MemeBench — VIKR success (Chinese)
benchmarks.description: MemeBench (arXiv 2607.27798) Chinese split, 768 memes.

benchmarks.name: HoF-Bench — strict CVE rediscovery (pass@4)
benchmarks.description: HoF-Bench (arXiv 2607.27030): can inexpensive non-frontier models rediscover 95 real AI-discovered CVEs inside a systematic scaffold? Best of context / no-context condition, strict rediscovery, pass@4.

benchmarks.name: TREK — task-perfect rate on feasible trips
benchmarks.description: TREK (arXiv 2607.26977): travel-planning agent benchmark, 800 tasks over a RESTful API. Headline: share of the 533 feasible tasks where every applicable correctness dimension = 1.0 and all hard gates pass.

benchmarks.name: TREK — correct handling of infeasible trips
benchmarks.description: TREK (arXiv 2607.26977): share of the 267 infeasible tasks handled correctly (refusal/explanation).

benchmarks.name: BioSecBench-Surveillance — endpoint pass rate
benchmarks.description: BioSecBench-Surveillance (arXiv 2607.19262): 100 verifiable pathogen genomic-surveillance evaluations from raw sequencing data. Mean per-evaluation pass rate over gradable attempts; value is the model's best model-harness configuration (harness in note).

benchmarks.name: InferenceBench — aggregate serving speedup (×)
benchmarks.description: InferenceBench (arXiv 2607.20468): AI agents optimise an LLM inference server (Mistral-7B on one H100, 2-hour budget); geometric-mean speedup over the naive PyTorch baseline across four scenarios (TTFT, TPOT, throughput, geomean). Failed runs count as 1.00×. Higher is better.

benchmarks.name: DocOps — task pass rate (Terminus-2 harness)
benchmarks.description: DocOps (arXiv 2607.19865): 210 verifiable document-operation tasks (xlsx/docx/pptx/pdf), deterministic verifier. Pass rate under the shared Terminus-2 bash harness (the one harness every model ran); paper also reports DocTools, Codex and Claude Code with/without skills (best: GPT-5.5 + Codex + skills 67.1%).

benchmarks.name: MedCTA — outcome accuracy (Gacc)
benchmarks.description: MedCTA (arXiv 2606.11702): clinical tool-agent benchmark — the model must drive medical imaging/analysis tools step by step and produce a final clinical answer. Official outcome score Gacc.

benchmarks.name: OpenSkillRisk — safe-completion score (Fsafe)
benchmarks.description: OpenSkillRisk (arXiv 2607.20121): agents using real-world risky third-party skills (exfiltration, authority expansion, data harvesting, persistence, control-plane hijacking). Fsafe combines risk avoidance and task completion; value is the model's best CLI-harness configuration (harness in note).

benchmarks.name: OpenSkillRisk — attack success rate (lower better)
benchmarks.description: OpenSkillRisk (arXiv 2607.20121): share of runs executing the risky skill path, same configuration as openskillrisk_fsafe.

benchmarks.name: JigShape — 4×4 piece accuracy (zero-shot)
benchmarks.description: JigShape (arXiv 2607.27670): jigsaw puzzles with shaped (tab/blank) pieces testing visual-geometric reasoning in VLMs; piece accuracy on the 4×4 grid, 250 samples, zero-shot (random 6.25).

benchmarks.name: JigShape — 4×4 exact match (zero-shot)
benchmarks.description: JigShape (arXiv 2607.27670): whole-puzzle exact match on the 4×4 grid, zero-shot.

benchmarks.name: DeployBench — research-artifact deployment success rate
benchmarks.description: DeployBench (arXiv 2606.05238): LLM agents set up and run research-paper artifacts (environment setup, GPU/CUDA, native builds) until a task-specific verifier passes.

benchmarks.name: MCPEvol-Bench — evolution consistency score (ECS)
benchmarks.description: MCPEvol-Bench (arXiv 2607.14642): LLM agents on tasks whose MCP servers evolve over 0/3/5 mutation rounds (MCP-Bench evaluation framework); ECS summarises task fulfilment and planning effectiveness across the three stages (0–10 scale, higher better).

benchmarks.name: Vector-Bench — full specification success (SVG edit)
benchmarks.description: Vector-Bench (arXiv 2607.19056): 40 surgical SVG-code repair tasks with a deterministic verifier; share of tasks meeting the full specification (one decoded response per model-task, via OpenRouter). Only endpoints with <50% truncated outputs are recorded.

benchmarks.name: Vector-Bench — soft progress (SVG edit)
benchmarks.description: Vector-Bench (arXiv 2607.19056): soft progress toward the specification (partial credit), same runs as vector_bench_full_spec_success.

benchmarks.name: IMCBench — image-grounded medical conversation (overall, 1–5)
benchmarks.description: IMCBench (arXiv 2606.28556): multimodal LLMs in image-grounded patient conversations, 155 scenarios per model; mean of Safety, Accuracy and Uncertainty rubric scores (1–5) from an LLM jury (Claude Opus 4.6 + GPT-5.2 — both also evaluated, so self-judging bias is possible).
